Package com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.vio.sim

Class QuestNavNTBridge

java.lang.Object
com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.vio.sim.QuestNavNTBridge
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public class QuestNavNTBridge extends Object implements AutoCloseable
The NetworkTables bridge: it publishes the topics a Meta Quest running QuestNav publishes, and services the commands the robot code sends it.

It uses the same protobuf adapters the vendor uses (FrameDataProto, DeviceDataProto, CommandProto, CommandResponseProto) instead of reimplementing the serialization. Sharing the adapter is what guarantees wire compatibility: if QuestNav changes the schema, this stops compiling instead of publishing bytes the robot code cannot read.

Topics

Schema of the QuestNav table

frameDataheadset → robotProtobufQuestNavFrameData
deviceDataheadset → robotProtobufQuestNavDeviceData
versionheadset → robotString
responseheadset → robotProtobufQuestNavCommandResponse
requestrobot → headsetProtobufQuestNavCommand

    • publishFrame

      public void publishFrame(QuestNavFrame frame)
      Publishes a frame with an explicit timestamp.

      The explicit timestamp is essential: the headset runs at 100 Hz and the robot cycle at 50, so every cycle publishes several frames. Without separating them in time, the robot code would see them as simultaneous and PoseFrame.dataTimestamp() --- which comes from the NetworkTables clock, not from the protobuf --- would be useless for dating measurements.

      Parameters:
      frame - the frame to publish.

    • flush

      public void flush()
      Pushes what was published this cycle onto the wire, without waiting for the NetworkTables timer.

      It is only needed when publishing as a network client: there the values cross a socket, and leaving them in the buffer until the next flush turns 100 Hz of frames into 10 Hz bursts.

    • publishResponse
